Volume 01 / The quiet revolution
01 / The woman behind the image

The world saw a face.
She was building a mind.

A life of exquisite contrasts. A woman of intuition, vision, and extraordinary experience.

Rita Rochd moved through international fashion and business, surrounded by the people, places and possibility the world calls success. Yet the most meaningful things she learned were often the things nobody could see.

Behind the beautiful image was someone studying human behaviour, recognising the distance between outward achievement and inward connection.

“Having everything people can see doesn’t mean you have all the answers within.”

The private edition / My Story
01 / Before the world knew her

I did not survive to merely exist. I survived to show other women what is possible.

Every chapter — intuition, glamour, loss, rebuilding, and the deeper return — was leading somewhere Rita could not yet see.

This story is not a formula for anyone else's life. It is the account of a woman whose experiences gradually brought her into a different relationship with her own voice, self-trust and personal freedom.

Chapter 01 / A girl with a vision
From Morocco to London

A vision beyond
what she could see.

From childhood, Rita carried a sense of possibility beyond the circumstances immediately around her. She describes an unusual sensitivity to people and the feelings beneath appearances, noticing things for which she did not yet have words.

Alongside that intuition was ambition: a belief that a larger world could exist even before she knew how to reach it. From Morocco to London, that instinct accompanied her into experiences she could not yet imagine.

“She didn't have a name for it then. She simply knew.”

Chapter 02 / Fashion and business
Behind the image of success

The world saw the glamour.

At a young age, Rita entered international fashion and business, travelling and moving among designers, royalty, celebrities, entrepreneurs and influential people. The photographs and extraordinary rooms told one part of the story.

Meanwhile, she was watching people. How power was carried. How businesses were built. What success could give, and what it could not. She noticed how often accomplished people relied upon someone they could trust beyond the public image.

“While the world saw a face, she was building a mind.”

Chapter 03 / The turning point
When the familiar life changed

When life asked a different question.

Behind the beautiful image, Rita's life was changing in ways almost no one could see. An abusive marriage was followed by a life-changing injury, operations, crutches, and years of disability. Eventually, she was told that she would never walk again.

Her marriage, career, financial security, support, independence, and the identity she had built were deeply affected. As familiar roles disappeared, a question remained: who are you when the life that once defined you is no longer there?

This part of Rita's story is shared with care: not as a universal lesson about disability, but as part of her individual experience.

A passage from the journey

“When I could no longer stand on my feet, I learned to stand in my truth.”

24years old
04 / Rebuilding while living with disability

Her first million.
Not her final transformation.

At the age of 24, while living with disability and rebuilding her life, Rita made her first million. Not after every difficulty had been resolved — during it.

It was a remarkable financial milestone. But what she began understanding was even deeper: money could change circumstances and achievement could alter what the world saw. Neither could replace the relationship she had with herself.

Her inner rebuilding involved recognising the quiet ways a woman can move away from herself, and reclaiming voice, boundaries, choice, dignity and self-trust.

06 / Why the Phoenix

Not the same woman.
Still herself.

Rita didn't choose the Phoenix only because it is a beautiful symbol. She recognised herself in the idea of loss, alchemy, rebirth and return.

The Phoenix Alchemy Method emerged from her lived experiences. Her story inspired the philosophy, but no woman's path must be a copy of hers. The work is about reconnecting with the truth that belongs to you.
